question: Which of the following figures has the greatest number of lines of symmetry?
solution:
A line of symmetry is a fold line along which the two halves of a figure coincide. For a triangle or quadrilateral, such a line must pass through vertices or side midpoints. Checking these possibilities gives the complete counts:

An equilateral triangle has 3 lines, each joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

A non-square rhombus has 2 lines, its diagonals.

A non-square rectangle has 2 lines, joining the midpoints of opposite sides. Its diagonals are not symmetry lines because its adjacent sides have different lengths.

An isosceles trapezoid has 1 line, perpendicular to its bases through their midpoints.

A square has 4 lines: its two diagonals and the two lines joining midpoints of opposite sides.

The greatest count is \(4\), so the answer is the \(\boxed{\text{square}}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
